title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MARIA'S TRUCK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Maria, a waitress from San Antonio, Texas.
For twenty years, she had one dream. Her own food truck.
And for twenty years, she had one excuse.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE EXCUSE
segments.quote: The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
segments.author: Franklin D. Roosevelt
lines: The excuse was fear. What if nobody came? What if she lost everything?
Then one night, her grandpa's old radio played a famous speech by President Franklin Roosevelt.
The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
Maria turned off the radio, and started a list.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: SOMEDAY
segments.quote: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: But the list sat in a drawer for months. Someday, she kept saying. Someday.
Rosa finally lost patience with her, which is funny, because Rosa is never on time for anything.
Her friend Rosa, who reads too many old books, sent her a line from Seneca, a Roman thinker:
While we are postponing, life speeds by.
Maria looked at the gray in her hair. Okay. Not someday. Saturday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE PORCH
segments.quote: Well done is better than well said.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: She couldn't afford a truck. But she could cook.
Her neighbor had a Ben Franklin calendar on his fridge. That month, it said:
Well done is better than well said.
So she stopped talking, and started selling tamales from her front porch.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE RAIN
segments.quote: Fall seven times, stand up eight.
segments.author: Japanese proverb
lines: The first Saturday, it rained. Nobody came.
The second Saturday, the tamales burned. The third, the city said she needed a permit.
Maria sat on the porch steps, soaking wet, ready to give up.
Her mother called, and reminded her of an old Japanese saying:
Fall seven times, stand up eight.
Maria got the permit. And she bought a bigger umbrella.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: ONE STAR
segments.quote: I've failed over and over and over again in my life. And that is why I succeed.
segments.author: Michael Jordan
lines: Then came her first online review. One star. Salsa too spicy.
She almost quit that night. But her nephew's old poster of Michael Jordan was still on the garage wall:
I've failed over and over and over again in my life. And that is why I succeed.
So she made two salsas. Mild, and brave. The brave one sold out.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TRUCK
segments.quote: Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement.
segments.author: Helen Keller
lines: One year later, Maria had saved enough for a used truck. Rusty, loud, and perfect.
On the side, she painted words from Helen Keller:
Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement.
Today, the line outside her truck goes around the block.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Face the fear. Start now. Just do it. Get back up. Learn from failing. Stay hopeful.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Face the fear. Start now. Stop talking, start doing. Get back up. Learn from every fall. And stay hopeful.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And try the brave salsa.
